plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 3: Polynomial and Rational Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single Cartesian graph showing a rational function together with the two asymptotes it approaches. The horizontal x-axis carries integer ticks from -5 to 5, the vertical y-axis carries even ticks from -12 to 12, and both are tipped with arrowheads. A dashed orange vertical line stands at x = 1 and runs the full height of the frame, labeled x = 1 in orange near its lower end. A dashed teal line of steep positive slope crosses from the lower left to the upper right, labeled Slant asymptote y = 3x + 1 above and right of the origin. The function is a solid dark blue curve in two branches. The left branch enters at the lower left pressed against the teal line, rises to a shallow turning point just below the x-axis near x = 0, then plunges off the bottom of the frame as it nears the orange line. The right branch descends from the top just right of x = 1, turns at a minimum near y = 9, and climbs away to the upper right, again closing on the teal line. Drawing the curve and both dashed lines on one set of axes lets the reader compare each branch against the boundary it hugs. The graph illustrates the case in which the numerator exceeds the denominator in degree by one, so the polynomial quotient supplies a slanted rather than horizontal end behavior.

interactionPlan.concept: A rational function whose numerator degree exceeds the denominator degree by one approaches a vertical asymptote near the denominator's zero and a slant (oblique) asymptote — given by the polynomial quotient — as end behavior.
elements: x-axis with arrowheads and integer ticks from -5 to 5, labeled x
y-axis with arrowheads and even ticks from -12 to 12, labeled y
dashed orange vertical line at x = 1 spanning the full frame, labeled 'x = 1' in orange near the bottom
dashed teal slant asymptote line y = 3x + 1 running lower-left to upper-right, labeled 'Slant asymptote y = 3x + 1' in teal above and right of the origin
solid dark blue curve, left branch: hugging the teal line at lower left, rising to a shallow local max just below the x-axis near x = 0, then plunging off the bottom as x → 1⁻
solid dark blue curve, right branch: descending from the top just right of x = 1, reaching a minimum near y = 9, then climbing upper right while closing on the teal line
movable probe point on the curve with coordinate readout (x, f(x))
orange guide showing vertical distance from the probe to the line x = 1
teal guide showing distance from the probe to the slant asymptote y = 3x + 1

interactions.label: x position of probe
interactions.teaches: Dragging the probe along the curve shows the distance to x = 1 collapsing (and f(x) blowing up) near the vertical asymptote, while the distance to the slant line shrinks toward zero at the far left and far right — two different boundaries governing two different regimes

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The dashed lines are not part of the function — the curve exists on its own, and the asymptotes are reference boundaries it approaches but (for the vertical line) never touches

demo_steps.title: Meet the curve
demo_steps.narration: Hide the dashed lines: the rational function alone is just two smooth blue branches with a gap. Nothing on the curve itself tells you where the boundaries are.

demo_steps.title: Add the asymptotes
demo_steps.narration: Show the combined view: the gap in the curve sits exactly at the orange vertical line x = 1, and both outer ends of the curve settle against the teal line y = 3x + 1.

demo_steps.title: Probe the vertical asymptote
demo_steps.narration: Drag x toward 1 from the left: the probe plummets and the orange distance-to-x=1 guide shrinks toward zero while f(x) runs off to -∞. The vertical asymptote controls the local blow-up where the denominator is zero.

demo_steps.title: Probe the slant asymptote
demo_steps.narration: Drag x far left or far right: the teal distance-to-slant-line guide shrinks toward zero as the curve straightens onto y = 3x + 1. The slant asymptote — the polynomial quotient — controls end behavior.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The same curve answers to two boundaries: the vertical asymptote x = 1 (from a zero of the denominator) dictates behavior near that point, while the slant asymptote y = 3x + 1 (the quotient polynomial) dictates behavior as x → ±∞.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Single Cartesian axes, x ticks at integers -5 to 5, y ticks at even values -12 to 12, both axes with arrowheads. Vertical dashed orange line at x = 1 full height, label 'x = 1' in orange near y ≈ -8. Slant dashed teal line y = 3x + 1 with its two-line label in teal to the right of the y-axis around y ≈ 5-6. Dark blue solid curve in two branches: left branch glued to the slant line at the lower-left corner, shallow turning point just below y = 0 near x = 0, then a steep dive off the bottom edge just left of x = 1; right branch enters from the top just right of x = 1, bottoms out near (1.5, 9), and exits upper right converging on the slant line. Probe point drawn as a filled dot on the curve with a coordinate label, an orange horizontal guide segment to x = 1, and a teal perpendicular guide segment to the slant line, each with its numeric length. In 'Asymptotes only' view the blue curve fades out and only the two dashed lines remain; guides hide when the corresponding layer is hidden.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for an x-value probe: the learner drags x along either branch, a point moves on the rational curve, and guide distances to x = 1 and y = 3x + 1 show why the vertical asymptote controls local blow-up while the slant asymptote controls end behavior.
- Toggle between curve-only, asymptotes-only, and combined views: the dashed vertical and slanted lines appear or disappear over the same axes, making clear that the curve can approach two different kinds of boundary without either dashed line being part of the function.

authoredContext:
To find the equation of the slant asymptote, divide 3 x 2 −2x+1 x−1. The quotient is 3x+1, and the remainder is 2. The slant asymptote is the graph of the line g(x)=3x+1. See the figure.

Slant Asymptote when f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0 where degree of p>degree of qby1.

Graph of f(x)=(3x^2-2x+1)/(x-1) with its vertical asymptote at x=1 and a slant asymptote aty=3x+1.

Case 3: If the degree of the denominator = degree of the numerator, there is a horizontal asymptote at y= a n b n, where a n and b n are the leading coefficients of p(x) and q(x) for f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0.
